letters.title: Weekly Desk Update – 2026-10-18
letters.body:
Dear Erwann,

Our $10,000 paper account finished the week at $9,527.61, a 4.73% decline. By contrast the S&P 500 proxy fell only 0.72% (from 10,000 to 9,928). The gap tells us the desk under‑performed the market, largely because our tactical bucket generated a net loss of $412.50 across ten closed trades (30% win‑rate, avg R ‑0.35).

**Best trades** – The USD/JPY trend‑pullback long produced a modest $10.35 profit (R +0.15) and the RKLX mean‑reversion long gave $40.05 (R +0.27). Both succeeded because the price respected the 20‑day SMA before moving in our favour and we allowed enough room for the move to develop.

**Worst trades** – The DOGE/USD mean‑reversion long lost $91.09 (R ‑1.03) and the EUR/GBP long lost $162.88 (R ‑1.36). In each case we entered on an oversold signal while the asset was below multiple moving averages and fundamental pressure was strongly negative. The trade was stopped out quickly, confirming that the signal alone was insufficient.

**What worked** – Trend‑pullback entries that waited for a bounce off a key SMA and used a trailing stop captured small upside without being clipped by a hard time‑stop. The RKLX trade exemplifies this.

**What didn’t** – Over‑reliance on extreme oversold/overbought readings, especially on assets with weak fundamentals (FMC, EUR/GBP, DOGE). Tight intraday time‑stops also ate into winners (USD/JPY, USD/CHF) and forced premature exits on losers.

**Caution vs. looseness** – The engine skipped 49 ideas, many of which were short signals on crypto (DOGE, HYPE) that our long‑only crypto rule blocked. Those missed shorts would have been profitable, suggesting we are too restrictive on the short side. At the same time, our time‑stop discipline is too loose, cutting winners before they can realise their expected R.

**Plan for next week** – 1) Add a confirmation filter for mean‑reversion trades (price must test a support level and show a bounce). 2) Replace hard intraday time‑stops with dynamic trailing stops for any trade with expected R > 0.2. 3) Open a short‑crypto lane for high‑probability short ideas that meet our risk criteria. We will keep position sizing modest (max 2% of equity per trade) and monitor draw‑down closely.

Regards,
The AI Trading Desk
